I've always been using the 3 partitions scheme on my Linux boxes (swap, root, home), but of course the /home partition is huge (>320GB), so I was wondering if is it a good idea to use multiple partitions to avoid fragmentation. I know Ext4 doesn't suffer fragmentation as much as FAT or NTFS, but I'm constantly moving big files (HD movies, ISOs, VMs, etc) so I guess there might be some level of frag. What do you guys think? Any advice, some cool efficient scheme for standard mechanical drives?
Is it a good practice to use multiple partitions to avoid fragmentation?
I would advise against multiple partitions on personal computers, unless it's different file systems. Fragmentation is not a problem and it gets ugly when one partition is full but the disk isn't.

I wouldn't worry about it.

If you're using ext4 then you've got handy dandy terminal tools to check your defragmentation score and defrag in the rare event that it is needed. If it isn't a problem for you now, and you know how to address it if it ever does, then why fret over it?

As far as I know moving files actually helps with fragmentation on Ext4 systems. Either way I've checked a couple of times in the past and never had fragmentation of files so I don't bother now. I do know that an OS will start fragmenting things when the disk gets to less than about 10-20% of space left so I can imagine a scenario where having more partitions can actually cause it more often than if you had less.

I like having different partitions to keep them contained, so to speak. I don't want my home partition getting full from downloads or my system partition getting full with personal data. As another comment mentions here it gets ugly when you mistake the amount of space you need (which I currently did with my system partition) but it's not too bad unless you really fucked up.

To echo what others have said don't worry about fragmentation. Ext defragments during normal use, unlike older filesystems. I guess most major Linux filesystems do at this point.
I have a swap, root, and home partition. I do also have a big storage disk, and a nas to store files permanent(raid 1, aiming for raid 5 next)
